content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: p99 decode latency > 3s for hosted API across us-west-2, streaming stalls increasing. Automated SLO alert triggered at 4335000000.

oncall-alex: seeing it on the graphs now. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~980ms over last 6m, p99 ~3.2s. streaming stalls/egress errors also up 8x.

sre-maya: confirmed, alerts show a correlated spike in kernel compilepath errors after the TRT/FlashAttention kernel rollout ~10m ago. rollout id: rollout-2026-03-trt8-kernel.

runtime-ian: I rolled the new kernel (+fused_flash_attention v2) to a small canary, looks like the compatibility matrix missed a codepath for kv-cache eviction under batching. repro: heavy streaming + long contexts triggers page faults in the new kernel path.

ml-raj: observed a significant increase in temp page faults and CPU spin on the decode worker. Could be a new allocation pattern in the fused kernel (FlashAttn fallback).

oncall-alex: impact: a subset of customers hitting streaming timeouts (client-side). SEs reporting live users getting stalled responses, some 504s. @support-jordan can you pull sample customer IDs?

support-jordan: pulling now. Early list: cust_zephyr, acct-alfred, growth-dash (3 accounts). Tickets inbound.

runtime-ian: mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel to previous image (safe, but requires rolling long-lived pods), 2) toggle runtime flag to force legacy attention kernels (fast toggle), 3) throttle batching to reduce eviction pressure.

sre-maya: recommend option 2 first (config flag) to avoid large rollout rollback. Can we flip `use_fused_flash_attn` -> false at runtime?

runtime-ian: yes we expose `use_fused_flash_attn` via config service. I'll prepare a rollout to toggle it for affected pools. Command: `curl -XPOST https://ops-config/api/v1/pools/us-west-2/patch -d '{"use_fused_flash_attn":false}'`

deploy-bot: Deploy started for config-change-4335000000 by runtime-ian. Canary: 5% pools. ETA ~120s. (reacted :rocket:)

oncall-alex: toggle now, push to canary only. monitor p95/p99 and streaming success rate.

sre-maya: rerouted a few requests to fallback region as safety: policy `fallback-low-latency` active.

(3m later)

runtime-ian: canary shows p95 back to ~150ms, p99 down to ~420ms. Streaming stalls reduced by 70%. Proceeding with staged rollout to remaining pools.

ml-raj: logging shows the eviction path now bypassing the fused kernel; kv-cache eviction rates normalized. Uploading logs to the thread: ```
[2026-03-15T12:05:03Z] worker-42 WARN kv_cache: eviction_ms=120 allocs=14 pagefaults=0
[2026-03-15T12:04:59Z] worker-42 INFO kernel: attention=legacy path enforced
```

runtime-ian: rolling to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over next 10m. Will pause if any regression.

support-jordan: customer notifications drafted. Will send templated update: "We're investigating increased latency; mitigation in progress; no data loss." @product-lucy want to review wording?

product-lucy: thumbs up to safety-first wording. Add ETA: "rolling mitigation across regions; next update in 30 minutes."

(10m later)

sre-maya: full rollout completed at 4335000180. Post-rollout checks: p95 ~140ms, p99 ~400-600ms depending on load. Streaming error rate returned to baseline.

oncall-alex: incident status -> contained. Next: root-cause and postmortem. Assigning to runtime-ian + ml-raj to own RCA.

ml-raj: initial hypothesis: performance regression introduced by a kernel-level optimization in fused FlashAttention that changes allocation alignment under certain batch+seq combos; triggers extra page landscaping on the compile path when paired with TRT 8 driver. We need to reproduce with a stress harness.

runtime-ian: action items: 1) reproduce with stress harness (priority), 2) add unit test for kv-cache eviction under fused path, 3) add runtime guard to auto-fallback when pagefaults > threshold, 4) prepare safe rollout checklist for next kernel release.

sre-maya: I'll schedule a hotfix branch policy for kernel rollouts to force gradual canary and automated p95/p99 gating.

oncall-alex: handoff to day team: keep monitoring dashboards for 6h. If p99 creeps >1s, page to oncall.

support-jordan: customers updated with a post-mitigation note. No escalations so far.

product-lucy: ops notes: need clearer pre-rollout gating in release docs. Will follow up in postmortem.

runtime-ian: logging collected and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/4335000000/ (links sanitized). I'll open a PR with reproduction and tests.

ml-raj: estimate for RCA + patch: 2 days. If test shows kernel bug, may need vendor engagement (TRT team) for a driver-side fix.

oncall-alex: thanks all. Marking incident as: contained -> monitoring. Will update status in incident tracker.

incident-bot: INCIDENT update: contained at 4335000180. Severity: sev2. Tags: kernel, trt, flashattn, streaming, paging, rollback-safe.

(Hand-off note)
oncall-alex: Handoff summary for day team (copy into oncall playbook): 
- What happened: TRT/FlashAttention kernel rollout caused a decode tail/paging regression under heavy streaming + batching.
- Mitigation: toggled `use_fused_flash_attn=false` (config rollback) to force legacy kernels, staged rollout completed.
- Impact: p95/p99 spikes, streaming stalls, several customer timeouts. No data loss.
- Next steps: reproduce, add tests, improve rollout gates, vendor coordination.

sre-maya: tagging owners: runtime-ian, ml-raj. Oncall rotation: @sre-maya for monitoring until 6h.

support-jordan: leaving notes in tickets for the affected customers.

product-lucy: will create the postmortem doc and link to RCA items.

oncall-alex: closing thread in 30m if no regressions. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
